items.feedback: Right — a loose body, soft eyes, forward ears, and a gentle tail curve are the classic calm and curious pattern. The key is to read the whole posture together, because tense posture or flattened ears would change the read entirely.

You got the stress signal: anxious and uncomfortable is the right read. To make it fully complete, add that the cat is likely asking for space or distance, because a lower body, tucked tail, and flattened ears usually mean 'please back off.'
Right — rapid tail-thumping and direct staring usually mean high arousal or irritation. The smart move is to pause, lower your movements, and let the cat decide whether to continue contact.

This is the wrong read for a slow blink. A slow blink usually means the cat feels safe and relaxed enough to trust you, and it is a friendly signal rather than a threat check. The wrong idea is treating a calm cat like it is on alert; when the body is loose and the eyes are soft, that is comfort, not danger.

summary: You correctly recognized the relaxed pattern in q1 and the irritation warning in q3. The main thing to fix is the difference between a calm slow blink and a tense, defensive posture: a soft, loose cat is usually safe, while a stiff body and flattened ears are the warning signs. Next time, read the whole posture first and ask whether the cat is choosing contact or space.
